body_ar:
حكم من سب اللوح أو الشريعة

ما موقف الشرع ممن قال للوح القرآن أف أو قال: عندما ذكرت له الشريعة \"يگلعها\" أعاذنا الله من الشر؟

بالنسبة لمن قال هذا إذا كان عاقلا ونوى به مقصوده كان بذلك خارجا من الملة كافرا نسأل الله السلامة والعافية، وإذا لم يقصده أو كان مغطى على عقله فأراد التضجر من القارئ من الطالب مثلا الذي يقرأ عليه، أو كان مغلوبا على عقله بالغضب أو نحو ذلك فإن هذا مما يعذر به ولكن لا بد من التوبة والإنابة وأن يعلم أنه قال أمرا عظيما،

والراجح في مثل هذا النوع أن المعتبر فيه النية، وقد ذكرت الخلاف في الماضي وذكرت قول العلامة محمد مولود رحمة الله عليه في الكفاف: أجمعت الأمة فيمن أجرى** على لسانه ضلالا كفرا أن ليس يحكم له بالرده** والنسفي عمدتي وعمده وهو وإن خالفه أجله** منها أبو الفضل عياض جله فاللفظ لا القصد وإن صح رعوا** وهكذا قرائن الحال لغوا

لكن الراجح من ناحية الدليل أن العبرة بالنية والقصد لقول النبي (ص):«إنما الأعال بالنيات وإنما لكل امرئ ما نوى» فكما لا يدخل الإنسان في الإسلام إلا إذا كان قاصدا له كذلك لا يخرج منه إلا إذا كان قاصدا لذلك، فالخروج منه كدخوله...

--------------------------------------------------------------

حكم من نقض عهدا مع الله

من نقض عهدا مع الله ما هي كفارته وهل هذا من نواقض الإيمان؟

ليس هذا من نواقض الإيمان لكن عهد الله يمين فمن قال علي عهد الله أن أصوم كذا أو أن أتصدق بكذا أو أن أقوم مثلا كذا من الليل فإنه حلف بذلك وعهد الله يمين كفارته كفارة اليمين بالله وقد قال الله تعالى: {فكفارته إطعام عشرة مساكين من أوسط ما تطعمون أهليكم أو كسوتهم أو تحرير رقبة فمن لم يجد فصيام ثلاثة أيام ذلك كفارة أيمانكم إذا حلفتم واحفظوا أيمانكم}.

--------------------------------------------------------------

حكم من يدعو غير الله، وتعليق على حديث الأعمى

ماذا تقولون فيمن يدعو غير الله عز وجل وإذا قيل له ادع الله قال: ادعه أنت؟

نعوذ بالله، هذا الشخص ينبغي أن ينصح وأن يبين له أن دعوة غير الله تعالى شرك، وأن الله أنزل فيه كثيرا من الآيات في القرآن وأنه خصه بسورة كاملة هي سورة الزمر التي فيها التحذير من دعوة غير الله، فإن الله يقول فيها: {تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتَابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ (1) إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ فَاعْبُدِ اللَّهَ مُخْلِصًا لَهُ الدِّينَ (2) أَلَا لِلَّهِ الدِّينُ الْخَالِصُ وَالَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ مَا نَعْبُدُهُمْ إِلَّا لِيُقَرِّبُونَا إِلَى اللَّهِ زُلْفَى إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ فِي مَا هُمْ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي مَنْ هُوَ كَاذِبٌ كَفَّارٌ (3) لَوْ أَرَادَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًا لَاصْطَفَى مِمَّا يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ} [الزمر] فلذلك لا يمكن أن يدعى أحد من دون الله وكذلك يقول فيها: {قُلْ إِنِّي أَخَافُ إِنْ عَصَيْتُ رَبِّي عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ (13) قُلِ اللَّهَ أَعْبُدُ مُخْلِصًا لَهُ دِينِي (14) فَاعْبُدُوا مَا شِئْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ قُلْ إِنَّ الْخَاسِرِينَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَأَهْلِيهِمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَلَا ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْخُسْرَانُ الْمُبِينُ}[الزمر] وفيها يقول الله تعالى: {ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا رَجُلًا فِيهِ شُرَكَاءُ مُتَشَاكِسُونَ وَرَجُلًا سَلَمًا لِرَجُلٍ هَلْ يَسْتَوِيَانِ مَثَلًا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ}[الزمر] وفيها يقول الله تعالى: {أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِكَافٍ عَبْدَهُ وَيُخَوِّفُونَكَ بِالَّذِينَ مِنْ دُونِهِ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ هَادٍ (36)} [الزمر]، وفيها يقول الله تعالى: {قُلْ أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ مَا تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ إِنْ أَرَادَنِيَ اللَّهُ بِضُرٍّ هَلْ هُنَّ كَاشِفَاتُ ضُرِّهِ أَوْ أَرَادَنِي بِرَحْمَةٍ هَلْ هُنَّ مُمْسِكَاتُ رَحْمَتِهِ قُلْ حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ يَتَوَكَّلُ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ (38)} [الزمر].

وبالنسبة لحديث الأعمى وإن صححه بعض أهل العلم إلا أن الذي يظهر لي أنه ضعيف لأن فيه أربع علل، علتان في الإسناد وعلتان في المتن،

أما العلتان اللتان في الإسناد فإنه من رواية شعبة بن الحجاج عن أبي جعفر عن عمارة بن خزيمة بن ثابت، وأبو جعفر هذا مجهول ولذلك قال الترمذي في السنن: عن أبي جعفر وليس الخطمي، العلة الثانية أن النسائي أخرجه فقال: عن عمارة بن زيد بن ثابت بدل عمارة بن خزيمة بن ثابت، وعمارة بن زيد بن ثابت مجهول لم أجد له ذكرا بعد طول بحث إلا ذكرا لا يبشر بخير وهو أن مالكا ذكر في الموطإ أن فتية من الأنصار تعاقروا الخمر فقتلوا أحدهم بالسكاكين فكتب مروان بأمرهم إلى معاوية فأمره أن يقيد منهم، ولم يسم هذا القتيل ولكن ابن حزم سماه في المحلى أنه عمارة بن زيد بن ثابت، وعلى هذا فإن الرجل الذي قتل في معاقرة الخمر لا يمكن أن تقبل روايته،

أما العلتان في المتن فإحداهما أنه فيه أن عثمان كان محتجبا ولم يعرف عن أحد من الخلفاء الراشدين أنه احتجب، بل هم يعلمون أن رسول الله (ص) قال: من ولي من أمر أمتي شيئا فاحتجب عنهم احتجب الله عنه يوم القيامة، ولم يحتجب أحد من الخلفاء الراشدين قط، ولم يكن لهم حارس ولا بواب، وكذلك الرسول (ص)، وعثمان بن عفان كان يعلم الناس الوضوء على باب المسجد كما ثبت ذلك في الصحيحين، وكان يذهب في الثلث الأخير من الليل إلى المسجد فيضطجع في مؤخرته يعلم الناس القرآن كما ثبت في الموطإ فكيف يحتجب عن الناس من هذه صفته،

الأمر الثاني أن فيه قوله: «اللهم شفعني فيه وشفعه في» فشفعني فيه معناه أن الرجل يريد أن يكون شافعا في محمد (ص)، وهذا ما لا يمكن أن يكون، لكن هذا يحمل على أن المقصود به أن الرسول (ص) على فرض صحة الحديث علمه هذا فالمقصود شفعني فيه معناه استجب دعائي له باستجابة الدعاء، وشفعه في معناه استجب دعاءه لي بأن ترد علي بصري، فعلى هذا يكون هذا من التوسل بدعاء الرسول (ص) وهو محل إجماع بين المسلمين لا ينكره أحد منهم، فيكون خارجا عن محل الاستشهاد أصلا وليس فيه أي استغاثة أصلا.
body_en:
The ruling on one who insults the writing-board or the Sharia

What is the position of the revealed law regarding one who said 'ugh!' to the writing-board of the Qur'an; or who said, when the Sharia was mentioned to him, 'yigliʿhā' — God protect us from evil?

As for the one who says this: if he is of sound mind and intended by it what it means, he is thereby outside the religion, an unbeliever — we ask God for safety and well-being. And if he did not intend it, or his mind was clouded over — so that he meant to express irritation with the reciter, with the student, for instance, who was reciting to him — or was overcome in his mind by anger or the like, then this is something for which he is excused; but repentance and turning back to God are indispensable, and he must know that he has said a grave thing.

The stronger view in this kind of case is that what counts in it is the intention. I have mentioned the disagreement in the past, and mentioned the words of the erudite Muhammad Mawlud, God's mercy be upon him, in al-Kaffāf: *The community is agreed, concerning one upon whose tongue there has run an error amounting to unbelief, that he is not judged to have apostatised — and al-Nasafi is my authority and his. And although one greater than him differed from it, namely Abu al-Fadl Iyad, the eminent one among them: it is the utterance, not the intention, that they took into account, where the utterance is established; and so they held the circumstantial indications to be of no account.*

But the stronger view from the side of the evidence is that what counts is the intention and the purpose, because of the Prophet's words, upon whom be peace: 'Deeds are only by intentions, and each man has only what he intended.' For just as a person does not enter Islam except when he intends it, so too he does not leave it except when he intends that; leaving it is like entering it...

--------------------------------------------------------------

The ruling on one who breaks a covenant with God

One who breaks a covenant with God — what is his expiation, and is this among the things that nullify faith?

This is not among the things that nullify faith. But a covenant with God is an oath. So whoever says 'I have God's covenant upon me that I will fast such-and-such, or that I will give such-and-such in charity, or that I will stand, say, so much of the night' has sworn by that; and God's covenant is an oath whose expiation (kaffārah) is the expiation of an oath by God. God, exalted, said: {Its expiation is the feeding of ten needy people from the average of what you feed your families, or clothing them, or the freeing of a slave; and whoever does not find [the means] — then a fast of three days. That is the expiation for your oaths when you have sworn. And guard your oaths} (Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:89).

--------------------------------------------------------------

The ruling on one who supplicates other than God, and a comment on the hadith of the blind man

What do you say concerning one who supplicates other than God, mighty and majestic, and who, when he is told 'supplicate God', says: 'You supplicate Him'?

We seek refuge in God. This person should be advised, and it should be made clear to him that supplicating other than God, exalted, is associating partners with God; that God sent down many verses about it in the Qur'an; and that He devoted a whole sura to it, namely Sūrat al-Zumar, in which is the warning against supplicating other than God. For God says in it: {The revelation of the Book is from God, the Mighty, the Wise (1). Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so worship God, making the religion sincerely His (2). Unquestionably, to God belongs the pure religion. And those who take protectors besides Him [say]: we worship them only that they may bring us nearer to God in nearness. Indeed, God will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, God does not guide one who is a liar and an ingrate (3). Had God intended to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed} [الزمر] (Sūrat al-Zumar 39:1–4).

Therefore no one may be supplicated besides God. He also says in it: {Say: indeed I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day (13). Say: God do I worship, making my religion sincerely His (14). So worship what you will besides Him. Say: indeed the losers are those who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss} [الزمر] (Sūrat al-Zumar 39:13–15). And in it God, exalted, says: {God sets forth a parable: a man belonging to partners at odds with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man — are the two equal in likeness? Praise belongs to God! But most of them do not know} [الزمر] (Sūrat al-Zumar 39:29). And in it God, exalted, says: {Is not God sufficient for His servant? Yet they would frighten you with those besides Him. And whomever God leaves astray, for him there is no guide (36)} [الزمر] (Sūrat al-Zumar 39:36). And in it God, exalted, says: {Say: have you then considered what you call upon besides God? If God intended me harm, could they remove His harm? Or if He intended me mercy, could they withhold His mercy? Say: God is sufficient for me; upon Him do those who rely place their reliance (38)} [الزمر] (Sūrat al-Zumar 39:38).

As for the hadith of the blind man: although some of the scholars have graded it sound, what appears to me is that it is weak (ḍaʿīf), because it contains four defects — two defects in the chain of transmission and two in the text of the report.

As for the two defects in the chain: it is from the narration of Shubah ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Jafar, from Umarah ibn Khuzaymah ibn Thabit — and this Abu Jafar is unknown, which is why al-Tirmidhi said in the Sunan 'from Abu Jafar', and not al-Khatmi. The second defect is that al-Nasai recorded it and said 'from Umarah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit' in place of Umarah ibn Khuzaymah ibn Thabit; and Umarah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit is unknown. After long searching I found no mention of him except a mention that bodes no good: namely that Malik mentioned in the Muwaṭṭaʾ that some young men of the Ansar drank wine together and killed one of them with knives, and Marwan wrote about their case to Muawiyah, who ordered him to exact retaliation from them. He did not name the one killed, but Ibn Hazm named him in al-Muḥallā as Umarah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit. On this basis, the narration of a man who was killed in a wine-drinking bout cannot be accepted.

As for the two defects in the text: one of them is that in it Uthman is screened off from the people, and it is not known of any of the rightly guided caliphs that he screened himself off. On the contrary, they knew that the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, said: 'Whoever is put in charge of any of the affairs of my community and then screens himself off from them, God will screen Himself off from him on the Day of Resurrection.' None of the rightly guided caliphs ever screened himself off, and they had no guard and no doorkeeper — and likewise the Messenger, upon whom be peace. Uthman ibn Affan used to teach people ablution at the door of the mosque, as is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs; and he used to go in the last third of the night to the mosque and lie down at the rear of it, teaching people the Qur'an, as is established in the Muwaṭṭaʾ. So how could a man of this description screen himself off from the people?

The second matter is that in it are the words: 'O God, accept his intercession for me and accept my intercession for him.' 'Accept my intercession for him' means that the man wants to be an intercessor for Muhammad, upon whom be peace — and this cannot be. But it is to be construed as meaning that the Messenger, upon whom be peace, taught him this — assuming the soundness of the hadith — so that the sense of 'accept my intercession for him' is: answer my supplication for him, by answering the supplication; and 'accept his intercession for me' means: answer his supplication for me, that You restore my sight to me. On this basis this is a case of seeking a means through the supplication of the Messenger, upon whom be peace, which is a matter of consensus among the Muslims that none of them denies. So it falls outside the point at issue altogether, and there is no seeking of rescue in it at all.

flags.context: أو قال: عندما ذكرت له الشريعة \"يگلعها\" أعاذنا الله من الشر؟
options: yigliʿhā — a Hassaniya expression of contemptuous dismissal, left untranslated
'let it be torn up' — a dismissive Hassaniya retort
flags.note: CRITICAL. A Hassaniya (Mauritanian dialect) phrase written with the letter گ, quoted by the questioner as the very words spoken. The Sheikh's whole answer turns on how contemptuous it is and on whether the speaker meant it — the difference between a ruling of unbelief and an excuse — so the strength of the English wording would, by itself, decide how the fatwa reads. It has deliberately been left untranslated and transliterated rather than guessed. The Sheikh's office must supply the sense before this article is published. The record also carries literal backslashes around the phrase (the addslashes artifact of style guide §11); they are preserved in body_ar and omitted from body_en.

flags.context: ما موقف الشرع ممن قال للوح القرآن أف
options: the wooden tablet on which the Qur'an is written
flags.note: In the Shinqiti tradition the lawḥ is the wooden board on which a student writes out a portion of the Qur'an for memorisation, and it is the central object of the maḥẓarah. 'Tablet' risks confusion with al-lawḥ al-maḥfūẓ, the Preserved Tablet. The rendering chosen keeps the object concrete, which matters because the Sheikh's excusing clause is about a teacher irritated by a student reciting to him.

flags.arabic: كان بذلك خارجا من الملة كافرا
flags.context: the first item as a whole
options: publish with a preface from the Sheikh's office
hold from publication pending the Sheikh's office
publish as an ordinary item in the creed series
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW REQUIRED (style guide §12). This item states a ruling of takfīr — that a person of sound mind who says these words intending them leaves the religion. It also states the conditions and the excuse at length, and the Sheikh's own preferred position is that intention, not the bare utterance, decides. Both halves must travel together: quoted alone, either half misrepresents him. Translated exactly as given, with nothing softened and nothing strengthened. The decision whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.arabic: وهو وإن خالفه أجله** منها أبو الفضل عياض جله
flags.context: the third line of Muhammad Mawlud's naẓm
options: and although one greater than him differed from it, namely Abu al-Fadl Iyad, the eminent one among them
and though the greatest of them differed from him in it — Abu al-Fadl Iyad, their most eminent
and he, though Abu al-Fadl Iyad, the greatest of them, differed from him in it
flags.note: The line is compressed to the point of obscurity: أجله and جله both mean 'the greatest/most eminent of them', and منها ('from it') has no clear antecedent in the printed text. What is certain is the substance — that Qadi Iyad differed from al-Nasafi's position, and that on Iyad's view the utterance decides and circumstantial indications are disregarded. A reviewer with al-Kaffāf should confirm the wording.

flags.arabic: وبالنسبة لحديث الأعمى وإن صححه بعض أهل العلم إلا أن الذي يظهر لي أنه ضعيف
options: publish with a preface from the Sheikh's office
hold from publication pending the Sheikh's office
publish as an ordinary item in the creed series
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW ADVISED (style guide §12). The hadith of the blind man is the single most cited proof text in the dispute over tawassul, and here the Sheikh grades it weak against scholars who grade it sound, sets out four defects in it, and then adds that even if it were sound it would prove only tawassul through the Prophet's supplication, which he says is a matter of consensus. All four defects and the concluding concession have been translated in full; dropping any of them would change what he is taken to have ruled. Note that the argument includes an accusation about a named narrator's death in a drinking bout, reported from Ibn Hazm.

flags.context: لقول النبي (ص):«إنما الأعال بالنيات وإنما لكل امرئ ما نوى»
options: read as الأعمال and translate 'deeds' (done here)
reproduce the defective spelling in the English
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. الأعال is a dropped-letter misprint of الأعمال in the most famous hadith in the corpus. The misprint is preserved in body_ar and the word read correctly in body_en, since there is no doubt what the text is.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

Three separate fatwas are published on this one page, divided in the source by rules of hyphens. The rules are preserved in both body_ar and body_en so the boundaries survive; the site should render them as three separate items. Each item's own heading is part of the source text and has been kept.
The first item breaks off with an ellipsis in the source ('فالخروج منه كدخوله...'). The ellipsis has been reproduced; it is not a truncation introduced in extraction.

The source supplies its own sura marker '[الزمر]' for each of the five Qur'anic passages in the third item, and its own verse numbers inside them. Those have been kept and the full house references added beside them.

The Sheikh's gradings in the third item have been carried exactly, including that he differs from 'some of the scholars' who graded the hadith of the blind man sound, and that his own verdict is given as what 'appears to me'. Nothing has been hardened into a settled ruling.
The lines of verse from al-Kaffāf are rendered as prose in italics per house style; the source marks the hemistich break with a double asterisk.
Source spellings preserved verbatim in body_ar: الأعال for الأعمال, بالرده for بالردة, and الموطإ (twice) alongside the usual الموطأ.
